_comment: Atlas-specific audit knowledge. Every entry here is a JUDGEMENT the scanners cannot make from evidence alone; each carries the reason it was made. Adding a path to silence a finding you have not understood defeats the audit.
_generated_globs: Vendored or machine-written: real files that ship, but reviewing them line by line is pointless. atlas-three.bundle.js is the vendored three.js build (rebuild via `npm run build:comfy-three` in ui/), and .graphifyignore already keeps it out of the knowledge graph for the same reason.
_provenance_docs: Dated records. They name files that were later removed and counts that were correct when written; that is the record doing its job. docs/DESIGN_RULES.md cites 'found live' evidence by path for every rule, so it is provenance throughout.
_foreign_path_prefixes: Paths in ANOTHER project's tree, named to say where a behaviour was mirrored from. Correct as written, can never resolve here.
_local_only_prefixes: Gitignored by design (CLAUDE.md): they do not survive a clone and are excluded from the published Registry archive. The scanners ask `git check-ignore` rather than trusting this list, so it is documentation of intent, not the mechanism.
_known_absent_symbols: Named in docs and/or implemented in the tree, deliberately NOT in NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS. A test pins AtlasPredictHiddenGeometry out of the mappings (off-menu research path). AtlasRenderFix and AtlasBlenderOrganicFill were deregistered and their wrappers deleted 2026-08-14; INSTALL.md and docs/ROADMAP.md name them to say they are GONE, which is correct prose about an absent thing.
_entry_point_dirs: A script here is invoked by a HUMAN or by CI, so its importer count proves nothing. Findings against these are reported separately and never reach CERTAIN.
_dynamic_loading_markers: A directory containing any of these reaches its own modules without an import statement. Every file under such a directory is capped below CERTAIN.
_protected_categories: Categories whose confidence is capped below CERTAIN regardless of evidence. A fixture is discovered by pytest, a DCC script is executed by Maya/Nuke/Blender out-of-process, a setup file is read by pip — none of which leaves a reference this scanner can see.
